title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for mood.

HPI: Patient is a 78-year-old male with a history of major depressive disorder, single episode. He reports a stable mood over the last several months. He denies significant changes in sleep, appetite, or interest in activities. He states he feels well and is continuing with his current routine.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Neuro: Negative
Psychiatric: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Negative

Medication List:
Sertraline 50mg daily

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Mood: Euthymic.
Affect: Full range, congruent to mood.
Speech: Normal rate and volume.
Thought Process: Linear and goal-directed.

Assessment:
Major depressive disorder, single episode. The patient is currently in full remission.

Plan:
1. Continue current medication.
2. Follow up in 3 months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed, 
R. Mensah, NP
October 14, 2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, in full remission (no HCC): F32.5.

distractors.why: The provider documents full remission: code the remission, not an active severity.
The remission is full, not partial.
